utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody. Madam Registrar, would you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-98-34-A, the Prosecutor versus Martinovic and Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. May I now call for appearances. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Appearing for the Prosecution is Norman Farrell, Ms. Marie-Ursula Kind, and Ms. Susan Grogan. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. May I turn to the Defence. Mr. Martinovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: Matt Hennessy here for Mr. Naletilic, along with Chris Meeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. For Mr. Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, I'm Zelimir Par, Defence counsel for Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I don't have the translation, but thank you. I have problems with the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear now the English channel? Can you hear the English channel? Can you hear the English booth now? Can you hear the English booth now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I hear noise in my earphone. Now can you hear me? Do the interpreters hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Okay. Now it's fine. Well, the last Status Conference in this case was held at the end of March, so we almost come to the end of the 120 days which are indicated by the Rules. First let me ask the appellants if they have any problem, any concerns, to raise relating to the appeal, to the detention conditions, and so on. May I ask counsel for Mr. Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we do not have anything to remark in relation to Vinko Martinovic's detention, and we have no special questions to raise today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. May I ask counsel for Mr. Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As to detention, we have no issues to raise today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you very much. Then I think we can move to the status of the case. First the question concerning the additional evidence we should deal with. As to the appeal of Mr. Naletilic, there's a motion that has been filed by Mr. Naletilic under Rule 115. A response has come in from the Prosecution and the Chamber will decide in due course on the motion. As to Mr. Martinovic's appeal, there has been a motion which has been disposed of, a second motion under Rule 115 is pending and will again be decided by the Bench in due course. I got just before coming here another motion which unfortunately I had no time to read because I got it five minutes ago, submitted by the Appellant Naletilic to present additional evidence pursuant to Rule 115. Well, first I would like perhaps to hear from the Prosecution if they were aware of this motion or just they received it today. I have to note that this motion comes very late, and as far as I can see, just having a very quick look at it, no leave is asked by the appellant to submit a motion so late -- I don't have now the figures exactly, but it must be more or less one year after the deadline for submitting bona fide motions in the case. I say more or less because I don't have the exact date in mind now. Well, I don't know whether the Prosecution wants to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, I noted under the Rules that were in force at the time the notice of appeal was filed, the Rules at that time indicated that there was 75 days. The Rules had been amended at the time of the filing of the notice of appeal in this case, so they were in force since that time. I have had the chance to review the motion, and I have also brought it to the attention of counsel for Mr. Naletilic that it might be advisable that they at least seek leave under the present Rules as the 75-day period has passed. And as far as I can read the motion, there wasn't leave sought, so I leave it for my learned colleagues, counsel for Mr. Naletilic, to indicate whether they intend to seek leave as well. But, yes, I would agree with Your Honour that that is the process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. May I turn to counsel for Mr. Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. I wanted to file the motion concerning new evidence prior to the conference today. I was aware of the need to request leave. I needed to confer with my co-counsel and also to get the timing of our acquisition of documents. My notes at home reflected that we received them well after the 75-day cut-off by the Rules in place at the time of the filing of the notice of appeal. With the leave of the Court, I will file a motion for leave to file this motion for additional evidence setting out specifically the dates when we required them, which I now have and which I did not have last week on filing the motion. I simply wanted the Prosecution to have as much notice as possible as to these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hennessy. I understand that you understand that leave has to be sought to submit this motion. I would suggest that you submit a detailed request seeking leave. I see there are several documents here submitted, and they should indicate what are the reasons why this motion comes so late and couldn't come earlier, specifically to the several sets of documents you are submitting. I don't think for -- it is necessary that you re-file the motion. I will consider that just a waste of paper. So just complement the motion by request for leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I think this is an acceptable procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And just for the Court's information, all those documents were recovered at the same time and, as I say, recovered after the 75-day cut-off. So I understand the Court's use of the word that they're late; however, our acquisition of these documents was after any former deadline for filing Rule 115 motions. And in that regard we have only within the last two weeks come into possession -- I say "we." Members of the Defence team have come into possession of documents on the order of 1500 pages of documents which I have not reviewed yet, I have not seen yet. But I simply tell the Court about this at this time in anticipation of possibly filing a third motion under Rule 115, that these documents, as I say, are -- we've only had them about two weeks. And additionally, my understanding is we may be receiving additional documents pursuant to the Prosecution's continuing obligation to provide relevant materials here in the near future as well which are separate from the documents we only recently acquired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: That's fine. I only want to draw your attention to the Rules and the fact that to submit motions under Rule 115 with a certain delay like this, you must show good reasons for doing so. So please be as detailed as possible in giving those reasons. Well, this, I think, takes care of the questions concerning the additional evidence in this appeal for the time being. There is one other matter we may briefly consider. That's the question of the protective measures concerning Witness NC. We're in a public meeting, so I would not of course disclose any names. I think we are in a position now to - after the last filing by the Defence of Appellant Naletilic - to make a decision on that. And therefore, I think that after the recess you will receive a decision on this. I think we have all the elements now to make a decision on this matter unless the parties want to raise anything in this respect. Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that we've covered it in the various filings. I don't think there's anything else I could add today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: That's fine. Prosecution, I understand, has nothing to add to this. Well, let me ask if there are any other matters that the parties want to raise at this stage in this appeal. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour. There's no matters pending related to any of the issues before you. I just wanted to raise one thing. I had the opportunity to mention to counsel for Mr. Naletilic, but I haven't had the opportunity to mention to counsel for Mr. Martinovic, that I just thought I'd inform them officially that last week I was informed that there are some new documents that have been placed in the Croatian state archive. I have not had the chance to see them, and they aren't in the possession of the Prosecution. But in light of the fact that I understand there were some additional documents which were not previously in the Croatian state archive, I just want to put the Defence on notice of that in case they feel it necessary to do any further investigations and review the documents. I have been informed that the documents relate to some of the events in Central Bosnia. I don't know whether they relate to the events in Mostar, whether they would even be relevant to this case, but I just thought I'd put you on notice. Other than that, Your Honour, I have nothing further to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farrell. Does the Defence have anything to say on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the very first information that we've received about this, so we would like to express our thanks and we have no comments for the time being. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hennessy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The only thing I can imagine perhaps maybe to do in the future is if the Registry resists approving an investigator to review the documents for us since we're not conversant in the language I'm sure the documents are in, then perhaps we'll seek court intervention. But apart from that, no. And I thank the Prosecution for so informing us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Okay, fine. If there are no other matters, I think we can adjourn. The Status Conference stands adjourned. ---Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at 4.36 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25
